subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw handle Codex app-server `account/chatgptAuthTokens/refresh` by returning a still-usable cached token within the upstream 10-second external-auth deadline, or should the project instead rely on upstream timeout configurability or broader runtime auth-deadline work?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the durable fix changes the OpenClaw/Codex auth contract and must preserve the recent revoked-token and identity-safety fixes while deciding whether cached-token reuse is acceptable for this callback.

options.title: Bridge Fast Path For Usable Tokens
options.body: Return safe still-usable OAuth credentials for app-server refresh callbacks and force a real refresh only when expiry, identity, or unauthorized recovery requires it, with focused Codex app-server and OAuth regression proof.

options.title: Wait For Upstream Timeout Configurability
options.body: Keep this issue open while coordinating an upstream Codex configurable external-auth timeout, accepting continued deployed failures until both sides ship and are validated.

options.title: Fold Into Runtime Deadline Work
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93952 as the first landing path, then re-check whether the exact 10-second external-auth callback is still reproducible before adding a separate bridge change.

recommendation.title: Bridge Fast Path For Usable Tokens
recommendation.body: Return safe still-usable OAuth credentials for app-server refresh callbacks and force a real refresh only when expiry, identity, or unauthorized recovery requires it, with focused Codex app-server and OAuth regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice spans auth runtime, provider routing, and security-sensitive token behavior, and recent adjacent review context already routes the auth-deadline tradeoff to this owner signal.
